title: Passing `platforms=[]` to the tag generators yields tags for the host platform
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

```python
from packaging import tags
list(tags.compatible_tags((3,), "cp3", []))
```
Expected: `[Tag('cp3', 'none', 'any'), Tag('py3', 'none', 'any')]`, only the platform-independent tags.
Actual: these come after a tag for every host platform: `py3-none-linux_x86_64`, `py3-none-manylinux_2_39_x86_64`, ... (41 tags on Linux x86_64).

`tags.cpython_tags((3, 11), abis=["whatever"], platforms=[])` and `tags.generic_tags("sillywalk", ["abi"], [])` should yield nothing, but yield a tag for each host platform. Only `platforms=None` (the default) should mean "detect the current platform". An explicitly empty iterable means no platforms.
acceptance: `compatible_tags`, `cpython_tags` and `generic_tags` given an empty `platforms` produce no platform-specific tags
Omitting `platforms` still uses the current platform
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
